Subject: Regional availability impact — immediate traffic redistribution steps

Hi Janelle / Acme Ops team,

We observed a regional networking incident affecting parts of US-east and APAC edge connectivity starting ~08:45 PDT this morning. Some API calls routed through those optics experienced elevated latency and a small percentage of 503s. EU customers on certain peering paths also saw intermittent tokenization errors for long sequences.

Immediate actions you can take to limit user impact:

1) Switch to a healthy region via the region routing header (temporary):
   - Add header: "x-redwood-region: eu-west-1" (or "us-west-2" for US traffic)
   - This will route requests away from the impacted egress points and preserve session KV cache where compatible.

2) Use our fallback model param for lower-latency responders: 
   - Query param: "model=redwood/compact-v1" or header "x-redwood-model: compact-v1"
   - Compact variants maintain semantic parity for short completion workloads and reduce request time.

3) If you manage DNS-based ingress, prefer explicitly pinned endpoints:
   - api.redwood.com -> api-eu.redwood.com or api-us-west.redwood.com

We attached a short text file with curl examples and a brief timeline PDF. Our SREs are actively rerouting internal ingress and working with the cloud provider on peering restores.

If you want us to perform the header swap on your behalf for traffic coming from your account, reply to this thread and we can coordinate a short maintenance window (no downtime expected) to apply the routing override.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is urgent and are prioritizing a full post-incident review.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — 2028-06-25 regional egress disruption

Hi Janelle — following up with a concise post-incident summary and actionable items. Thanks for patience while we completed the internal RCA.

What happened (short):
- 08:43 PDT 2028-06-25: A peering configuration rollback at cloud-provider X caused asymmetric routing through several US-east and APAC edge POPs. This resulted in increased tokenization error rates for long sequence requests and higher 5xx rates for some customers.
- 08:45–09:30: Redwood SREs applied temporary ingress routing overrides to shift traffic to us-west-2 and eu-west-1; observed error rates fall back to baseline by 09:05 for most customers.
- 09:12: We posted the initial notice and provided header/curl examples.

Impact: Short-lived increased latency and a small portion (<1.2%) of requests returned 500/503 across affected regions. No customer data was exposed.

What we changed / recommended for customers:
- We implemented per-account header overrides for impacted customers (including ACME-4512) during the incident window.
- We are publishing a permanent guidance doc on preferred region hints and model fallbacks for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Customer actions you can take (for future resilience):
- Add a region hint header after your retry/backoff logic: "x-redwood-region" with preferred healthy region.
- Use model fallbacks for long-running requests: "compact-v1" for shorter context windows, and rehydrate to full model when KV cache present.
- For Private deployments, ensure route preference is pinned to secondary egress when primary peering is degraded.

Deliverables and follow-ups from Redwood:
- Postmortem (internal + customer redacted) link: https://drive.redwood.com/postmortems/2028-06-25-region-impact
- Incident timeline PDF attached (incident-timeline.pdf)
- Reroute command snippets: reroute-command-snippets.txt
- Support contact for escalation: SRE Escalations <sre-escalations@redwood.com>

We are also proposing two platform changes in the next sprint:
1) An API flag "region_preference=automatic" that enables automated safe failover to the next healthy region when latency crosses 95th percentile thresholds.
2) A runbook automation to auto-apply temporary account overrides based on health signals and customer opt-in.

If you need us to keep the header override in place for an additional maintenance window while you validate, let me know and we'll coordinate an exact window.

Apologies again for the disruption — we will share the redacted postmortem within 48 hours and our mitigation timeline.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
